prompt: Gentle, slow movement therapy for seniors at home, NOT martial arts. The same woman, same studio, same clothes and lighting. She moves slowly and smoothly from the pose in the first frame to exactly the pose in the last frame, in one continuous motion, nothing else. The weight settles onto the rear leg and the front foot slides forward to rest on its heel, toes up. Both hands float forward, the front hand at shoulder height and the other near the front elbow, as if holding a lute. Spine vertical. She stays TALL the whole time: her hips remain high, her knees are only softly unlocked (a slight bend of a few degrees, never a squat, never a lunge, never a deep stance), each knee stays above its own foot, the back heels stay on the floor, the spine is vertical, shoulders relaxed, chin level, calm gentle face, natural breathing. Static locked camera, no camera movement, no zoom, no cuts, full body always in frame from head to feet, feet visible on the floor, background unchanged.
